When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn to harness magic from the shadows. See chapter 10 of the Player's Handbook for the general rules of spellcasting and chapter 6 of this book for the subtlety spell list.

Cantrips

You learn two cantrips of your choice from the subtlety spell list. You learn another subtlety cantrip of your choice at 10th level.

Spell Slots

The Subtlety Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

For example, if you know the 1st-level spell command and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast command using either slot.

Spells Known of 1st-Level and Higher

You know three 1st-level subtlety spells of your choice.

The Spells Known column of the Subtlety Spellcasting table shows when you learn more subtlety spells of 1st level or higher. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 7th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one of the subtlety spells you know with another spell of your choice from the subtlety spell list. The new spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your subtlety spells. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a subtlety spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier
